Go Rural India

Font catalogue

Twenty-four faces. Group 1 can only ever be the hero wordmark, because a script cannot carry thirteen card titles legibly. Group 2 can carry every heading, so each shows both the wordmark and a real card title.

Every typeface here is embedded directly in this file, so what you see is the real font. The previous sheet linked to Google Fonts and the font files were blocked in the viewer, which is why several cells were silently falling back to Times. That is fixed.

Group 1: scripts, hero wordmark only

These replace only the big "Go Rural." Everything else stays Fraunces. Judge them on whether they sit happily beside the rickshaw illustration and the red ring, not on readability, since nobody has to read a logo.

Group 2: display faces, every heading

These carry the hero, the scroll headline, section headings and all thirteen card titles. The card title under each sample is the real test: if it looks weak or fussy there, the whole services grid will.

Give me a number from each group, for example "1 and 10" for a Great Vibes wordmark over Fraunces headings, or a single number from group 2 for no script at all. 22, 23 and 24 are worth a look: all three were drawn for Devanagari as well as Latin, so they carry an Indian typographic lineage none of the others do.
